order_equivalence.argument: For node n the baseline produces, per row: [end_nodes[i], weights_ab[i] for i ascending with start_nodes[i]==n] ++ [start_nodes[j], weights_ba[j] for j ascending with end_nodes[j]==n]. The candidate concatenates forward incidences (indices 0..E-1) and reverse incidences (indices E..2E-1) and stable-sorts by source. For a fixed source n, all forward indices (< E) sort before all reverse indices (>= E), and stability preserves ascending edge order within each group. Both incidence orders are therefore reproduced exactly, including the within-row forward/reverse interleaving question: for edges i=(u,v), j=(v,u), u's row is [v@i-forward, v@j-reverse] in both schemes because i < E+j; v's row is [u@j-forward, u@i-reverse] because j < E+i. Self-loops contribute forward then reverse in both; parallel/duplicate edges are kept distinct by stability; empty rows give repeated pointer values in both. bincount counts equal mask sums; cumsum(int64) equals the baseline's chained int64 adds (max total 2*edge_count <= intp_max-1 by the guard, no overflow).

guard_domain.note: For node_count >= 2**60 the pointer/bincount allocations exceed numpy's size limit and raise ValueError('array is too big'), which the helper's except MemoryError does not catch, so it escapes instead of returning None. Measured on numpy 2.4.6: the fallback's first statement np.zeros(node_count+1, int64) raises the identical ValueError type and message, so end-to-end observable behavior (exception type/message) is unchanged; only the traceback gains the helper frame. Domain is unreachable from real flows (node_count = node_points.shape[0], so a real array of that size must already exist). For allocations within numpy's limit but beyond RAM the fast path may die by OS OOM rather than MemoryError; the baseline loop is strictly heavier in time and memory at those sizes, so no candidate-specific regression. Cosmetic hardening option: reject node_count > intp_max//8 to keep the entire admitted domain inside the MemoryError-only contract.

amendment_review.reviewed_commit_title: Amend CSR guard: admit int32 endpoints via exact upcast
amendment_review.diff_scope_verified: helper diff confined to the endpoint dtype branch (int64 pair admitted unchanged; int32 pair admitted iff node_count <= int32max, upcast via astype(np.int64) once; everything else refused) plus start_i64/end_i64 renames through the size/range checks and try block; the sort/gather/return logic is byte-for-byte unchanged. Companion changes: int32 L0 cases, int32_realdata L1 case rename, corrected/new manifest hashes, benchmark probes.

upcast_exactness.argument: The original builder emits int64 neighbors from ANY signed integer endpoint dtype: its output conversion np.array(python_list, dtype=np.int64) widens each endpoint scalar exactly (int32 -> int64 is bijective), so output dtype was already int64 and values are exactly the int32 values. The candidate's whole-array astype(np.int64) is elementwise-exact, commutes with the stable gather ((A.astype(int64))[order] == A[order].astype(int64)), and bincount/pointer/range checks depend only on values, which the upcast preserves. Ordering logic is dtype-independent. Therefore candidate(int32) == original(int32) bit-for-bit on the whole admitted domain.
empirical: Direct verification of the widening claim itself (which the new L0 relies on implicitly, since it compares candidate(int32) against oracle(pre-upcast) inputs): oracle(raw int32 inputs) == oracle(int64-cast inputs) on 400 random graphs, dtype and bytes

candidate(int32) vs oracle(raw int32): 85 exhaustive 2-node int32 multigraphs (<=3 edges), reciprocal-edge interleavings in both edge orders hand-checked, aliased start==end self-loops, aliased ab/ba weights, strided views, negative strides, read-only arrays (unmutated, outputs owndata/writable), empty int32 arrays at node_count 0/1/5
campaign L1 int32_realdata (cited, not re-run) exercises the fast path end-to-end with bit-identical arms

boundary_choice.analysis: The node_count <= int32max bound is safe and defensible but conservative, not the maximal admissible domain. Exactness would hold for any node_count: the endpoint range check (max < node_count) is what keeps values valid and is dtype-independent, and the upcast is exact regardless of node_count. The bound's only effect is that int32 inputs with node_count in (int32max, intp_max] take the fallback, which produces identical output. Inclusive boundary: node_count == int32max is admitted; refusal at int32max+1 is pinned by L0 and re-probed here. Side benefit: within the admitted int32 domain, node_count <= int32max keeps the baseline's per-node `start_nodes == node` python-int comparisons within int32-representable values (not required for equivalence, but tidy). Untestable corner: admitted configs with node_count near int32max need >= 17GB for pointer/bincount in BOTH paths (equivalent resource behavior; L0 cannot execute them; refusal-side boundary checks are cheap and pinned).

resource_window.analysis: The int32->int64 astype copies execute in the guard section BEFORE the try/except MemoryError, so an OOM during upcast would propagate instead of falling back. Transient cost is 16 bytes/edge; the fallback needs 40-70+ bytes/edge of Python-list growth, so there is no realistic regression - same theoretical class as the base review's OOM caveat. No change required.
